issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the error of the greedy composition by iterating a per-composition Kenney–Laub bound but writes the exponent as $(d+1)^T$ with $d = 2q+1$. The cited Padé/Newton–Schulz bound gives exponent $q+1$ per composition (e.g., for $d=3$: $1-p_3(x)=\frac{(1-x)^2(x+2)}{2}$, while $\frac{(1-x^2)^4}{1+p_3(x)}\approx 0.19 < 0.31 = 1-p_3(1/2)$ at $x=1/2$), so the displayed intermediate inequality is false as written and the chain does not prove the stated bound $(q+1)^T$; with the exponent corrected to $(q+1)^T$ the chain ends exactly at the theorem's stated bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $(d+1)^T$ by $(q+1)^T$ in the two displayed estimates of the proof (matching the per-composition exponent of the cited Kenney–Laub bound and the theorem statement); the remaining chain is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem theorem:convergence is invalid as written (its penultimate displayed estimate is false); the theorem's stated quadratic ($d=3$) and cubic ($d=5$) rates themselves remain true after the one-symbol repair, so no advertised guarantee is lost.
issues.title: False exponent in the error chain proving the convergence theorem
issues.why_classification: A local one-symbol correction to an estimate; the theorem's statement, both advertised convergence rates, and every downstream claim survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For $p(x)=\frac{s}{8}(15-10s^2+3s^4)$ with $s=x/u\in[t,1]$, $t=\ell/u$, one has exactly $1-p_5(s)=\frac{(1-s)^3(3s^2+9s+8)}{8}$, so $\max_{[\ell,u]}|1-p(x)|=\frac{(1-t)^3(3t^2+9t+8)}{8}>(1-t)^3$ for every $t\in(0,1)$ (e.g., $t=1/2$: $0.207>0.125$). The Kenney–Laub estimate invoked supports at most $\max|1-p|\le(1-t^2)^3\le 8(1-t)^3$, so the final displayed bound $\max|1-p|\le(1-\ell/u)^3$ is false, and the concluded certificate $|p^\star-p|\le2\epsilon_{\text{double}}$ at the switch threshold $\ell/u\ge1-\epsilon_{\text{double}}^{1/3}$ does not follow (the honest constant is about $5\epsilon_{\text{double}}$, or a threshold $1-(2.5\,\epsilon_{\text{double}})^{1/3}$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last displayed bound by the valid estimate $\max_{[\ell,u]}|1-p(x)|\le\frac{(1-\ell/u)^3(3(\ell/u)^2+9\,\ell/u+8)}{8}\le 2.5(1-\ell/u)^3$ (or the cited theorem's $(1-(\ell/u)^2)^3$ form), and restate the certificate with the corresponding constant or a slightly lower switch threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The certificate justifying the early-return branch of Algorithm alg:remezdeg5 (and the prose claim that in that regime $p^\star$ equals the returned polynomial up to double-precision epsilon) is unsupported; with a corrected constant the branch still returns a polynomial within $O(\epsilon_{\text{double}})$ of the optimum, so the algorithm's behavior and all experiments are unaffected.
issues.title: False constant in the certificate for the near-degenerate Remez shortcut
issues.why_classification: A contained constant-level correction of one estimate; the shortcut, the algorithm, and every experimental claim survive with a slightly weaker constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed recursion defines $q_t(x)=(p_t\circ\cdots\circ p_1)(x)/x$ but also sets $q_0(x)=x$; the step $(p_{t-1}\circ\cdots\circ p_1)(x)=x\,q_{t-1}(x)$ then fails at $t=1$, since it demands $q_0(x)=x/x=1$. Taken literally, the recursion gives $q_1(x)=x\,h_1(x^4)$ instead of $h_1(x^2)$, so the claimed identifications $\bm R_t=r_t(\bm X)$ and $\bm Q_t=q_t(\bm X)$ fail at the base step (the algorithm initializes $\bm Q_0=\bm I$, and $\bm R_1=\bm X^\top\bm X$ is a function of $\bm X^\top\bm X$, not an odd polynomial of the rectangular $\bm X$; $r_1(x)=x^4$ is undefined for rectangular $\bm X$ under the paper's own convention). The algorithm's final guarantee $\bm X\bm Q_T=(p_T\circ\cdots\circ p_1)(\bm X)$ is in fact true, but the written derivation does not establish it.

failure_location.quote: It is clear by induction that $\bm R_t = r_t(\bm X), \bm Q_t = q_t(\bm X)$, and $\bm X \bm Q_T = (p_t \circ \cdots \circ p_1)(\bm X)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $q_0\equiv 1$ (so that $x\,q_0(x)=(p_0\circ\cdots)(x)=x$) and carry out the induction with the factors evaluated as functions of $\bm X^\top\bm X$ (i.e., $\bm R_t=\mV\rho_t(\mSigma)\mV^\top$ with $\rho_t(s)=s^2\hat q_{t-1}(s)^2$, $\bm Q_t=\mV\,\hat q_t(\mSigma)\mV^\top$); the displayed chain then proves $\bm X\bm Q_T=(p_T\circ\cdots\circ p_1)(\bm X)$ verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The correctness derivation of Algorithm alg:fastapply is invalid as written (its base case contradicts its own definition and its 'polynomial of a matrix' identification uses the wrong basis); the algorithm's stated input–output contract is nonetheless true, and the runtime claims are unaffected.
issues.title: Inconsistent base case in the fast-apply correctness derivation
issues.why_classification: A one-line base-case fix plus a notational clarification fully restores the derivation; the algorithm, its input–output guarantee, and all cost claims are preserved.
